chunks: And ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated from Yaḥyā al-Azraq, who said:
I said to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: “I performed four rounds of tawaf and became tired. Should I then pray its rakʿahs while I am sitting?” He said: “No.”
I said: “And how does a man pray salat al-layl if he becomes tired or feels weakness while he is sitting?” So he said: “A man performs tawaf while sitting.”
So I said: “No.” He said: “Then pray the two of them while you are standing.”

key_terms.أَسَابِيعَ: rounds of tawaf; here referring to completed circuits/sets
key_terms.رَكَعَاتِهَا: its rakʿahs, meaning the prayer attached to the tawaf
key_terms.طُفْتُ: I performed tawaf, meaning circumambulation of the Kaʿbah
key_terms.فَتْرَةً: a period of weakness or lethargy

ai.seo_question: Can the two rakʿahs of tawaf be prayed while sitting if a person becomes tired?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal ruling concerning the prayer associated with tawaf when a person becomes fatigued. The Imam عليه السلام rejects performing the two rakʿahs of tawaf sitting in this case and directs that they be performed standing, while also referencing the concession of performing tawaf sitting.
